effect: An AI donor's bilateral aid no longer goes to a country it is fighting or sanctioning. Each month an AI donor sends a quarter of its aid line directly to its top two recipients, ranked by their funding gap x (0.4 + relations scaled 0 to 1), checking only its diplomatic competency and the caps, so an enemy still scored 0.4 of a friend's weight. Measured on a one-year run of this game version: at day 365, 7 donor-recipient pairs were bilateral aid to a country the donor sanctions or is hostile to, 6 of them aid to North Korea. LC7 closed this for the multilateral split; now the bilateral ranking applies the same test before choosing the two recipients: a country is skipped when the donor is fighting it (the game's own belligerency test: an active conflict in its hostilities phase with the two on opposite sides) or when the donor is a sender in an active sanctions regime against it. The next-ranked country takes its place, so the donor's aid budget is unchanged. The monthly payment of an AI-governed donor's existing bilateral commitments also drops a commitment to such a country (the commitment is removed, so the donor's budget and the recipient's aid income stop counting it), so aid stops the month a donor sanctions or fights it rather than at its next budget review; that month's share is not paid. Commitments of a government the player runs are unchanged. Real-world behaviour: donors suspend or reroute official aid to governments they sanction or fight (OECD DAC practice; aid to Russia and Belarus after 2022, to Myanmar after 2021; from memory). Day-0 effect: measured on day 30 of a new game, no AI donor's top two bilateral recipients is a country it sanctions or fights (0 of 4.65 bn a month), so nothing moves at the start; the rule bites when sanctions or wars begin in play (7 such pairs at day 365 in the audit run). No recalibration: aid is a monthly flow and no starting stock or rating is built from it. No new saved state.
